hints: Compare the three diagrams carefully. Look at the size of the white vacuole and whether the grey protoplast is pressed firmly against the wall (cell Q) or pulling away from the wall (cell R).

Remember that a higher % sugar solution means a more negative (lower) water potential outside, so water leaves the cell by osmosis. Which cell has clearly gained water and which has clearly lost water?
walkthrough:
**Observe what happened to each cell**

Look side by side. Cell Q has a very large vacuole and the protoplast is pushed tightly out against the wall, so it has taken up water and is turgid.

Cell R has the protoplast shrinking and pulling away from the cell wall with a tiny vacuole, so it has lost water and is plasmolysed. Cell P is in between.

**Link sugar concentration to water movement**

Water always moves by osmosis from higher (less negative) water potential to lower (more negative) water potential.

A dilute 1% sugar solution has a high, less negative water potential, so water moves in. A concentrated 10% sugar solution has a low, more negative water potential, so water moves out.

**Match cells to solutions and check the conclusion**

Since all cells started the same, the turgid cell Q must have been in the most dilute 1% solution where water entered, and the plasmolysed cell R must have been in the most concentrated 10% solution where water left.

That makes option C the only correct conclusion.

options.A: Cell P is not fully equilibrated. It has a smaller vacuole than turgid cell Q, showing net water movement has occurred, so inside and outside are not at the same concentration.
options.B: This swaps the terms around. Cell Q is turgid, not flaccid, and cell R, not cell P, is the plasmolysed cell with the protoplast pulling away.
options.C: Correct. Cell Q is the most turgid with the largest vacuole, so it gained the most water by osmosis from the highest water potential solution, the 1% solution.
options.D: Opposite is true. Cell R lost water and plasmolysed, so water moved out. That means the outside solution was more concentrated and had a more negative water potential than inside.
